_readme: What the user is told changed. Policy and format: docs/tasks/whats-new.md. Add an entry in the same PR as the change; ids only go up and are never reused. 5 is skipped (a retired device test entry): the next id is 29.

entries.text: Marlow's routine jobs (the nightly ideas, tidying its memory, checking your inbox) now follow the day you set in Settings, under Your day. Check-ins can be turned off there.
Voice mode, where you talk to Marlow and hear its replies, now works in the Android app too.
You can take a photo from inside the app and send it to Marlow: tap + next to the message box and choose Take photo.
Marlow now tells you what changed after an update, like this. Past changes are always in Settings, under What's new.
You can now attach up to 6 photos to one message. Choose several at once from your library, or add them one at a time with the camera or paste.

Pairing a new device now uses a QR code or link instead of a six-digit code, and Unpair now also cuts that device off on Marlow's side, so a lost phone can be shut out. Devices you've already paired stay paired.

In the web app, Settings now has a Voice section: pick the voice voice mode reads replies in, and tap one to hear it first. These are the browser's own voices; the iPhone app keeps its own, better voices.

On an iPhone using the web app from the home screen, a reply you're watching no longer flashes a blank "Marlow has something for you." banner. If you lock the phone just before a reply lands, its notification can come up to about 15 seconds late.

Marlow's own files on the box (its memory, character, schedule and scripts) moved from the claude-assistant folder to marlow-identity, in the same home folder. Nothing in them changed and conversations carry on. If something of yours names the old folder, point it at the new one; the update lists any of Marlow's files that still do.

In the web app, voice mode now reads replies in Phonon, a natural voice made on your phone. The first time, it downloads the voice (about 65 MB) from Hugging Face; after that it works without downloading again. If you picked a voice in Settings, under Voice, choose Automatic to hear Phonon. You can also pick from 25 Phonon voices there; the default is Alfie.

In the web app, pairing now has a Scan QR code button that reads the code with your camera, so the app installed on your home screen can pair itself instead of the code opening in your browser. The camera is used only to read the code, and nothing is saved.

Getting started with Marlow on a new install now goes one step at a time, and Marlow keeps its place: a question on the way no longer ends the setup, and a step you skip or leave for a while moves on by itself.

You can now reply to a reminder. Before, Marlow had no idea which reminder you were answering, because it doesn't run when one goes out. Now it sees any it sent since you last talked, so "remind me again Friday" works.

Marlow now keeps a proper to-do list. Tap the checklist next to the lightbulb to see it: tick things done, snooze them, drop them, or tap one to talk about it. Ask Marlow to add anything, with a time if you want a reminder.

When a to-do with a time comes due, Marlow reminds you in the chat, and if you don't act on it, again a day later until it's done, dropped or snoozed. Turn the repeat off in Settings, under Repeat reminders daily, or just ask. After this update Marlow also moves your existing to-dos onto the list once, and tells you what it moved.

Marlow may suggest to-dos it notices, from your email for example. They show under Marlow suggested and never remind you until you accept them. Marlow asks about the important ones, and once more if one is still waiting two days later.

You can put your to-dos in your own order: drag a row, or use Move in its ⋯ menu. Every device shows the same order, and you can ask Marlow to move one. New items and ones whose due date changes still find their place by date.
In Chrome on Android, pulling down no longer reloads the page and closes what you had open.

Settings is tidier: your avatar and voice are at the top, and server details, Unpair and the app's build are now under Server connection and About at the bottom. About also lists the open-source software Marlow is built on.
On Android, the microphone and voice mode buttons have proper icons, and dictating shows a stop button to end it.
Press and hold one of Marlow's replies and choose Read aloud to hear it in the voice you picked in Settings. Tap Stop reading to end it.

You can now choose the model Marlow runs on, in Settings under Model: Sonnet or Opus. Opus has the best judgment and uses your plan's limits about twice as fast, and your scheduled jobs use it too. Thinking is now called Think time: Quick, Balanced or Thorough.
Marlow names your to-dos by what they are, in replies and in your morning brief, instead of codes like "t13".

On a computer, Marlow's replies now share one notification. Waking it after a while shows one "new" count instead of a toast for every reply you already read on your phone, and opening Marlow clears it.
You can attach any file to a message: tap + and choose Choose File. Marlow reads PDFs, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files and anything in plain text, and tells you when it can't open one.
Files you send are kept with your conversation for 30 days, like photos, so you can open them again from the message. Marlow itself only reads them during the reply.
Share to Marlow from other apps. On iPhone, choose Marlow in the share sheet. On Android, install Marlow to your home screen first, then it appears when you share.
